publication.title: Earthquake — real USGS observations
publication.description: Eleven scientific activities with 12,160 real USGS events; measured local Docker execution through the AkôFlow daemon.
publication.readme:
# Earthquake: real USGS observations

Run the eleven activities of the [Pegasus Earthquake workflow](https://github.com/pegasus-isi/earthquake-workflow) on CPU through the AkôFlow local executor. The original scientific scripts are preserved at commit `a31920b7b0bb0cfb30241ffd2566d935847e34a1`, with their MIT license in `scripts/upstream/`.

## Run

Install Docker and Go, then run from this directory:

```sh
./prepare.sh
./run.sh
```

The bundle includes a snapshot of 12,160 actual California seismic events of magnitude ≥3 from 2000-01-01 through 2025-12-31. Preparation requires internet for the container and Python packages, builds the Python environment and verifies the bundled catalog hash. The query, event count, retrieval time and SHA-256 are recorded in `data/catalog-provenance.json`. If no snapshot exists, preparation downloads it and rejects empty or potentially truncated results. Subsequent preparations reuse that exact snapshot. To deliberately refresh it, remove both `data/catalog.csv` and `data/catalog-provenance.json` before preparation. USGS may revise historical observations; preserve these two files together when sharing an experiment.

All execution activities run in Docker with networking disabled. The `fetch` activity verifies and stages the catalog downloaded during preparation; it does not make a new network request. The remaining ten activities run the unchanged upstream scientific programs. No tasks use simulated durations or fabricated observations. The runner uses two simultaneous containers; allow 4 CPU cores, 8 GiB RAM and 5 GiB free disk as a starting local capacity, rather than a measured minimum.

The DAG fans out from the catalog into pattern analysis, mapping, anomaly detection, DBSCAN clustering, statistical aftershock estimation, hazard assessment and gap analysis. Three dependent visualization activities consume the derived reports and the catalog. All file handoffs are declared in `workflow.yaml`.

The hazard grid uses 2-degree spacing to keep the local example manageable. This is coarser than the upstream 1-degree default and changes the spatial resolution of the calculation. Aftershock estimation uses the upstream default statistical mode; this bundle does not claim to train an ML model. The upstream hazard and aftershock models are illustrative scientific computations, not validated operational forecasts.

Outputs in `outputs/` include the catalog, six JSON reports, four PNG visualizations, a SHA-256 manifest and per-activity start/end times and logs. `./validate.sh` verifies artifact hashes, report errors, PNG decoding, event count and duplicate IDs.

## Daemon and Desktop

If the daemon binds to a LAN address, add `-api-url http://<daemon-host>:8080/akoflow-api` to the command below.

After preparation, with a local Docker-enabled AkôFlow daemon and `AKOFLOW_API_TOKEN` configured:

```sh
go run ../../tools/daemon-local -root ../.. -example scientific-workflows/earthquake -wait=false
```

This registers the local environment, scope, topology and the same eleven-activity DAG. It submits a real run and prints its ID for inspection in Desktop. Pegasus and HTCondor are not required by this adaptation.

## Provenance

- Upstream source and adaptation: `data/upstream.json`.
- Scientific code and license: `scripts/upstream/`.
- USGS service: <https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/>.
- Frozen observations and retrieval record: `data/catalog.csv`, `data/catalog-provenance.json` (bundled observation snapshot).
- Other workflow candidates: [research notes](RESEARCH.md).

## Measured local execution

Validated on 2026-11-15: **11/11 activities**, **12,160 actual USGS events**, four decoded PNGs and six parsed scientific reports. Total observed activity span: **475.44 seconds** with two concurrent Docker slots. Hazard assessment alone took **454.49 seconds**. These are wall-clock measurements on the shared execution host, not isolated performance benchmarks. See `evidence/local-run.json` for activity times, image ID, query provenance and artifact hashes. The standalone executor was tested; A real daemon execution was subsequently submitted; see `evidence/daemon-run.json` for its current recorded status and identifiers.

## Captured daemon execution

The measured daemon execution completed all 11 activities in 407.72 seconds. This publication preserves its native plan, observations, attempt logs and recorded file digests. The daemon reclaimed intermediate workspaces after consumption; final PNGs and terminal JSON reports remain on the execution host. The captured image is a local build alias; it has not been uploaded to a public registry. Reproduction on another host requires building the Dockerfile from the source bundle and assigning the captured image tag.

Source bundle: https://github.com/UFFeScience/akoflow-examples/tree/AKO-31/scientific-workflows/earthquake

This publication uses the Hub configured in this installation (the LAN instance), rather than claiming a publication on hub.akoflow.com.
